summary:
Your legs are too straight on the forehand, so your arm does the work instead of your body.

**What I made:** A highlight reel of your top 5 rallies by shot count. I found 18 rallies in total, and the longest ran 13 shots. I also made a breakdown of your forehand topspin at 56.4 s.

**What to work on first:**
1. **Bend your knees more.** At contact your knee angle is 157°. Fan Zhendong is at about 132° on the backhand and 114° on the forehand. Ma Long's forehand is 126°. Aim for about 125-135°. Your other strokes ranged from 135° to 166°, so the problem shows up most when you are rushed.
2. **Keep your stance steady.** Your stance width swung from 1.36 to 2.74 shoulder widths across your strokes. Hold it at about 1.8 to 2 shoulder widths so you can load into the same base each time.
3. **Open your elbow a little more.** At contact your elbow is 128°, and the pros' forehand elbows run from about 144° to 173°. Ma Long is 169° and Fan Zhendong is 161°. Let the arm extend forward and up through the ball instead of staying folded.

**Keep:** Your finish is long and extended across your body. That is a good sign that you accelerate through the ball.

**Drill:** Shadow-swing 20 forehands in front of a mirror. Start with your knees bent to about 130°, rotate your hips first, and finish high at eye level.

breakdown.headline: Sit lower, swing with your legs
breakdown.grip: Keep a relaxed shakehand grip, with the index finger lightly on the blade and a firm squeeze only at contact.
breakdown.stance: Your knees are at 157° at contact and your stance is about 1.8 shoulder widths. Sit to about 125-135° and keep your feet wide and steady.
breakdown.swing_path: Start with the bat low and behind your hip, then swing forward and up, driven by the legs and waist rather than the arm alone.
breakdown.contact_point: Meet the ball in front of your body at the top of the bounce, with your elbow open from 128° toward about 145° or more.
breakdown.follow_through: Finish high and across your body, then recover quickly to a balanced ready position with your knees still bent.
